summary: Official Afghanistan land-affairs, Ministry of Justice PRMIS/PMS, national-portal, and Helmand/Lashkar Gah administrative references were reviewed. The current PMS shell and anonymous API gate were inspected, but access was denied outside Afghanistan and no safe anonymous parcel ID plus polygon response was qualified. No sample GeoJSON was written.
custodian: National custodial roles are evidenced for the Ministry of Urban Development and Housing's geodesy/cadastre/deeds directorate and the Ministry of Justice PRMIS/PMS. A Helmand urbanism-and-land office lead is evidenced, but a city-specific public cadastral registry or local parcel service was not verified.
requests: Separate English and Dari/Pashto first-party discovery queries, official source-page inspection, PMS current JavaScript/configuration inspection, and anonymous geolocation/setup API requests are recorded in the city record. No login, credentials, CAPTCHA/Cloudflare bypass, private token, unsafe-field request, or TLS exception was used.
safeFieldAllowlist: stable native parcel identifier only if source-proven
full polygon geometry only when safely returned
scopeLimits: The WUP point [31.5875236725305,64.3627107337945] and population 188936 persons are preserved.
The PMS geolocation block and unavailable anonymous setup response concern only that exposed service route and are not citywide absence evidence.
No unsafe land-record fields were requested or retained.
No citywide polygon completeness, current anonymous API, CRS, native identity, or update cadence was verified.
Packet completion is not source integration/admission.
uncertainty: A supported in-country or authenticated Ministry of Justice/MUDH workflow may expose additional property or cadastral data, but it was outside anonymous safe research scope.
The Helmand local office references establish an administrative lead, not a qualified public parcel-vector source.
